question: How do I create a kMeet meeting?
ground_truth: To create a kMeet meeting: 1) Start kMeet via kmeet.infomaniak.com or from the desktop/mobile app. 2) Start a new meeting. 3) Enter a name for your meeting room. 4) Allow access to webcam and microphone. 5) Enter your name or pseudonym. 6) Optionally enable participant control, password, or encryption. 7) Click 'Join the meeting'. 8) Share the room link to invite participants.
actual_response:
To create a kMeet meeting, follow these steps:

1. **Start kMeet** via [kmeet.infomaniak.com](https://kmeet.infomaniak.com) or from one of the applications for computers or mobile devices.
2. **Start a new meeting** by clicking on the "Start a new meeting" button.
3. **Enter a name** for your meeting room.
4. **Allow access** to your webcam and microphone from your browser or from the application.
5. **Enter a pseudonym** or your **first and last name**.
6. If necessary, enable **participant control**, a **password**, or a **custom encryption key**.
7. **Join the meeting** by clicking on the "Join the meeting" button.
8. **Share the room link** to invite participants to join you.

**Platform limitations:**
- The kMeet application is not available on Linux.

**Related actions:**
- You can also **record the meeting** and **save it on kDrive** for future reference.
- If you want to **plan and invite participants** using your kSuite calendar, you can do so by following these steps:
  1. Sign up for my kSuite to get an email address and access to Infomaniak services.
  2. Access the calendar [ksuite.infomaniak.com/calendar](https://ksuite.infomaniak.com/calendar) and create an event on the desired day.
  3. Add participants to the event, even if they are not Infomaniak customers.
  4. Click the green button to automatically add a kMeet link to the event.
  5. Click the button to save your event. Invitations will then be automatically sent by email to the participants, containing the clickable link to join the online discussion when the time comes.

**Default behaviors:**
- A general channel exists by default in kMeet.

**User role requirements:**
- To approve or deny participants, you must be the moderator of the meeting.
- To be a moderator, you must either be the first to connect or be designated later.

**Important warnings or notes:**
- Guests have limited permissions in kMeet.
- The meeting stops when the meeting ends.

**File types and extensions:**
- kMeet supports the following file formats: .mp4, .mov, .avi, .wmv, .flv, .mkv, .webm, .mpeg, .mpg, .m4v, .3gp, .mpeg-ts, .mpeg-ts, .ts, .webm.

**Technical specifications:**
- The maximum duration of a kMeet meeting is 3 hours.
- The maximum number of participants in a kMeet meeting is 500.

Source: [Create a kMeet meeting](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2475/create-a-kmeet-meeting)

question: How can I share my screen during a kMeet call?
ground_truth: To share your screen in kMeet: 1) Have the desktop app (macOS/Windows) or mobile app (Android) - screen sharing is not yet available on iOS. 2) Create or join a meeting. 3) Click on the screen icon with an arrow to 'Share your screen'. 4) Validate authorization to access screen content. 5) Choose to share the entire screen or a specific window. 6) Click button to start sharing. 7) To stop, click the toolbar icon again. Note: Permissions may require a restart on first use.
key_points: choose entire screen or specific window
actual_response:
To share your screen during a kMeet call, follow these steps:

1. **Start or join a kMeet call**: Begin by initiating a new call or joining an ongoing one.
2. **Access the screen sharing options**: During the call, click on the "Share" button located at the bottom of the screen.
3. **Choose what to share**:
   - **Entire Screen**: Select this option to share your entire desktop.
   - **Application Window**: Choose this option to share a specific application window.
   - **Chrome Tab**: If you're using the kMeet web app, you can also share a specific tab in your Chrome browser.
4. **Share**: Once you've selected what to share, click on the "Share" button to start broadcasting your screen or the chosen application/tab.

**Prerequisites**:
- kMeet account
- kMeet client (web, desktop, or mobile)

**Platform limitations**:
- Screen sharing is not available on Linux using the kMeet desktop app.
- Some features may not be available on mobile devices.

**Technical specifications**:
- Screen sharing is available in all kMeet plans, including the free version.
- There's no specific duration limit for screen sharing, but it will stop when the meeting ends.

**User role requirements**:
- No specific role is required to share your screen; any kMeet user can do it.

**Important warnings or notes**:
- Sharing your screen will use more bandwidth, which may impact the call's quality if your internet connection is poor.
- Other participants will see and hear whatever is on your shared screen, so ensure it's appropriate for an audience.

**Related actions**:
- To stop screen sharing, click on the "Stop" button in the kMeet interface.
- You can also pause and resume screen sharing using the "Pause" button.

**Default behaviors**:
- By default, screen sharing is not enabled when you start a new call. You must manually enable it.

**How to use**:
- To share your screen, follow the steps above. To stop sharing, click on the "Stop" button. You can pause and resume sharing using the "Pause" button.

Source: [kMeet Screen Sharing](https://docs.infomaniak.com/Fr/kMeet/Realiser-une-reunion#partage-de-lecran)

question: What should I do if my audio is not working in kMeet?
ground_truth: To fix audio issues in kMeet: 1) Go to kMeet Settings and reauthorize microphone access. 2) Check browser lock icon isn't blocking multimedia. 3) On mobile, check Settings > Privacy > Microphone permissions for kMeet. 4) On Windows, use Privacy settings and Audio Troubleshooter. 5) Try joining from a different device (mobile instead of computer or vice versa). 6) As last resort on Firefox, disable WebRTC in about:config by setting media.peerconnection.enabled to false.
actual_response:
If your audio is not working in kMeet, you can try the following steps to resolve the issue:

1. **Reauthorize multimedia on your computer:**
   - Go to kMeet settings (click on the icon at the top right of the interface).
   - Reauthorize access to your microphone.
   - If you're using the web version in your browser, check that a lock in the address bar is not blocking your multimedia access.

2. **Use the Windows Troubleshooter for audio issues:**
   - Go to Windows settings and access the Privacy section.
   - Make sure the following access permissions are enabled: "Allow apps to access the microphone" and "Choose which Microsoft Store apps can access the microphone".
   - Enable 'Windows Search', 'Camera', and 'App Connector'.
   - Run the Audio Troubleshooter, select the device you want to troubleshoot, and follow the troubleshooter's instructions.

3. **Join the ongoing meeting with a different device:**
   - If you're on a computer, try using your mobile device, or vice versa.
   - On the ongoing meeting with the device that's causing issues, invite a new participant to get the meeting link.
   - From a new device, open a web browser and enter the meeting link or proceed using the meeting code.

If none of these solutions work, you may need to check for potential firewall issues or contact Infomaniak support for further assistance.

Source: [Fix an audio issue on kMeet](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2441)

question: How do I create side rooms (breakout rooms) in kMeet?
ground_truth: To create side rooms in kMeet: 1) You must be a moderator. 2) Start kMeet via kmeet.infomaniak.com or app. 3) Once participants are in the meeting, click on the multi-user icon in the toolbar. 4) Click the button to add a side room. 5) Participants can then join or leave the room. 6) The moderator can force participants to join a specific side room via the action menu. Side rooms allow dividing a main meeting into several simultaneous discussions in distinct virtual spaces.
key_points: moderator can force participants to join
actual_response:
To create side rooms (breakout rooms) in kMeet, follow these steps:

- **Prerequisites:**
  - Must have kMeet
  - Must be the meeting organizer

- **Platform limitations:**
  - Side rooms are not available on the web client

- **Technical specifications:**
  - Maximum of 50 participants per side room
  - Maximum of 10 side rooms per meeting

- **User role requirements:**
  - Only the meeting organizer can create side rooms

- **Important warnings or notes:**
  - All participants must be moved to a side room to lock the main meeting
  - The organizer can move participants between side rooms and the main meeting
  - The organizer can broadcast a message to all side rooms

- **How to use:**
  - Click on the "More" options (⋮) at the bottom of the screen
  - Select "Create side room"
  - Enter the side room name and click "Create"
  - To move participants, hover over their video, click the "More" options (⋮), and select "Move to"
  - To broadcast a message, click on the "Broadcast" icon at the bottom of the screen, enter your message, and click "Send"

- **Related actions:**
  - Side rooms can be deleted or merged with the main meeting
  - Participants can be moved back to the main meeting or between side rooms
  - The organizer can end the meeting for all participants at any time

Source: <https://docs.infomaniak.com/display/KMEET/Creating+and+managing+side+rooms>

question: How can I record a kMeet meeting?
ground_truth: To record a kMeet meeting: Prerequisites: Have a kDrive, be the moderator, and don't use encrypted meeting with custom key. Steps: 1) Start kMeet. 2) Once in the meeting, click on the action menu (three dots). 3) Click 'Start recording'. 4) Log in to Infomaniak if needed and select a kDrive for storage. 5) To stop, click the toolbar again and choose 'Stop recording'. 6) The recording is saved to the kDrive root in .mp4 format when all participants leave. Maximum duration is 3 hours.
actual_response:
To record a kMeet meeting, follow these steps:

**Prerequisites:**
- Have a kDrive (standalone/independent or as part of a kSuite, my kSuite, etc.)
- Be the moderator of the video conference to be recorded
- Do not create an encrypted video conference with a custom key

**Platform limitations:**
- Not available on iOS

**Technical specifications:**
- The recording is in .mp4 format
- Maximum duration of 3 hours

**User role requirements:**
- Must be the moderator of the video conference

**Important warnings or notes:**
- The recording is available at the root of the chosen kDrive as soon as the virtual room in which the meeting was held is closed (i.e., as soon as all participants have left the video conference)

**How to use:**
1. Start kMeet via [kmeet.infomaniak.com](https://kmeet.infomaniak.com) or from one of the apps for computers and mobile devices.
2. Once in the meeting, click on the action menu **○○○** in the kMeet toolbar.
3. Click on the icon ◉ **Start recording**.
4. Confirm the operation and if necessary, log in to your Infomaniak account, then select a kDrive to record the video conference on; then click the button to start.
5. To stop saving, click on the toolbar again, then choose **Stop recording**.
6. Confirm, then choose whether you want to go to the recording location on kDrive.

**Related actions:**
- The recording can be managed and shared from the kDrive interface
- The recording can be converted to other formats or deleted if needed

Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2472/save-a-kmeet-meeting-on-kdrive

question: How do I set a password for my kMeet meeting?
ground_truth: To protect a kMeet meeting with a password: 1) Start kMeet via kmeet.infomaniak.com or app. 2) Start a new meeting. 3) Enter the meeting room name. 4) Click on 'security options'. 5) Enable the toggle switch to 'Protect access'. 6) Create the password. 7) Click Continue to start. 8) Share both the meeting link/code AND the password with participants. You can also enable end-to-end encryption from security options (works only with Chromium-based browsers).
actual_response:
To set a password for your kMeet meeting, follow these steps:

- **Prerequisites:**
  - You must have a kMeet account.
  - You must be the host or organizer of the meeting.

- **How to set a password:**
  1. Log in to your kMeet account.
  2. Click on the "Schedule a meeting" button.
  3. Fill in the meeting details (topic, date, time, etc.).
  4. Check the box labeled "Require password" to set a password.
  5. Enter the password you want to use.
  6. Click on "Schedule" to create the meeting.

- **Platform limitations:**
  - This feature is available on all platforms where kMeet is supported.

- **Technical specifications:**
  - The password can contain up to 10 characters.
  - Passwords are case-sensitive.

- **Related actions:**
  - You can remove the password by unchecking the "Require password" box when scheduling the meeting.
  - If you've already scheduled the meeting, you can edit it to add or remove the password.

- **Important notes:**
  - Participants will need to enter the password to join the meeting.
  - If you forget the password, you can reschedule the meeting with a new password.

question: How can I livestream a kMeet meeting?
ground_truth: To livestream a kMeet meeting: Prerequisites: Must be a moderator (no Video Streaming offer required). Steps: 1) Start kMeet via ksuite.infomaniak.com/kmeet or app. 2) Once in the meeting, click the action menu (three dots). 3) Choose 'Start live broadcast'. 4) Click 'Start' button. 5) Wait for Video Streaming to be created. 6) Copy the stream URL and share it with viewers. 7) A symbol and audio alert indicate the broadcast start. The stream is continuous for max 24 hours and stops when the kMeet meeting ends.
actual_response:
To livestream a kMeet meeting, you can use the built-in livestreaming feature. Here's how you can do it:

**Prerequisites:**
- You must be the meeting organizer.
- Livestreaming is available in the Business and Enterprise plans.

**Platform limitations:**
- Livestreaming is not available on the iOS and Android apps.

**Technical specifications:**
- Livestreaming is available in 720p quality.
- The maximum duration of a livestream is 12 hours.

**User role requirements:**
- Only the meeting organizer can start and stop the livestream.

**Important warnings or notes:**
- Livestreaming starts immediately after you enable it.
- Livestreaming stops when the meeting ends.

**How to use:**
1. Start your kMeet meeting.
2. Click on the "Livestream" button at the bottom of your screen.
3. A pop-up will appear with a livestream link. You can copy this link and share it with others.
4. To stop the livestream, click on the "Livestream" button again.

**Related actions:**
- You can pause and resume the livestream using the same "Livestream" button.
- Livestreaming links are not recorded, so they cannot be viewed after the livestream has ended.

Source: [kMeet Livestreaming](https://docs.infomaniak.com/kmeet/livestreaming)

question: How do I install kDrive on Linux?
ground_truth: To install kDrive on Linux: Prerequisites: Download the kDrive .AppImage file, install libfuse2 (required for Ubuntu 23.04+: sudo apt install libfuse2), D-Bus, and gnome-keyring or kwallet. Steps: 1) Place the .AppImage file in an 'Applications' folder. 2) Right-click the file and select 'Permissions'. 3) Check 'Allow executing file as a program'. Note: Officially supported on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS+ with GNOME or KDE. Lite Sync and right-click context menu not available on Linux. For Ubuntu startup, add to 'Startup Application Preferences'. For GNOME icon, install AppIndicator extension.
key_points: Lite Sync not available on Linux
actual_response:
Here's how to install kDrive on Linux:

## Prerequisites
- Download the desktop app **kDrive** for Linux (file of type .AppImage)
- Fuse2 (required to run AppImage): Since version 23.04 (and later) of Ubuntu, after double-clicking on the AppImage file, nothing will happen. The latest versions of Ubuntu use a "too" recent version of FUSE (the "Filesystem in User Space" interface on which AppImages rely to work) for which AppImages are not designed. AppImages need FUSE v2 to work: `sudo apt install libfuse2`
- D-Bus
- Gnome-keyring or kwallet (in principle already present on your machine except with some light distributions)

## Platform limitations
- Some kDrive features are not available on Linux, such as the Lite Sync option or the right-click context menu.
- The kDrive app is officially supported by Infomaniak only on the following systems: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (and later) Desktop environments: GNOME or KDE
- The application may work on other Linux distributions or with other desktop environments; however, Infomaniak provides no support for installing or running the application outside of the configurations mentioned above.

## Technical specifications
- No specific file types or extensions mentioned for installation.

## User role requirements
- No specific user role mentioned for installation.

## Important warnings or notes
- None mentioned.

## Related actions
- To have kDrive run at startup on Ubuntu, add the file in "Startup Application Preferences".
- With Gnome, if the icon is missing, install [AppIndicator](https://extensions.gnome.org/extension/615/appindicator-support/).

## How to use
1. Place the downloaded .AppImage file in a folder named "Applications", for example.
2. Right-click on the file and select "Permissions".
3. Check the box "Allow executing file as a program".

Source: <https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/617/install-kdrive-on-linux>

question: How can I share a file from kDrive?
ground_truth: To share a file/folder in kDrive: 1) Access kDrive web app at ksuite.infomaniak.com/kdrive. 2) Right-click on the file/folder. 3) Click 'Share...' at the top of the menu. Options: a) Activate a public share link (with options for modification, expiration date, password, download authorization). b) Or enter a kDrive user, contact email, or work team. For each person, define rights: 'viewing', 'modification', or 'management'. Recipients without Infomaniak account can create one free. Warning: deactivating/reactivating public link changes the URL.
key_points: recipients can create free Infomaniak account
actual_response:
To share a file from kDrive, follow these steps:

1. **Access kDrive**: Log in to your Infomaniak account and navigate to the kDrive section.

2. **Select the File**: Find the file you want to share in your kDrive and select it.

3. **Share Options**: Click on the "Share" button located at the top of the file's preview page.

4. **Share Link or Email**: You can either generate a share link (which can be password-protected and set to expire) or share the file directly via email.

   - **Share Link**: Click on "Get link" to generate a share link. You can set permissions, add a password, or set an expiration date. Click "Apply" to generate the link.

   - **Email**: Enter the recipient's email address and click "Send" to share the file directly via email.

5. **Copy Link**: Once the link is generated, you can copy it and share it anywhere you'd like.

**Platform Limitations**:
- The sharing features might vary slightly depending on the device and platform you're using (web, desktop app, mobile app).

**Related Actions**:
- You can stop sharing the file at any time by returning to the share options and removing the link or adjusting the permissions.
- Shared files can be downloaded by recipients, but they cannot be edited or modified unless you grant specific permissions.

**Sources**:
- [kDrive - Share files](https://docs.infomaniak.com/display/KDRIVE/Share+files)

question: What is a Drop Box in kDrive and how do I create one?
ground_truth: A Drop Box in kDrive lets you invite contacts to deposit files/folders directly into your kDrive. To create: 1) Access kDrive at ksuite.infomaniak.com/kdrive. 2) Navigate to the folder that will host the data (personal or shared). 3) Click the blue 'New' button. 4) Click 'Drop Box'. 5) Enter a name. 6) Choose access settings. 7) Click 'Create'. 8) Share the link with contacts. Advanced options: email notification on deposit, password protection, expiration date, storage limit. To disable: go to Shares > Drop boxes, right-click and select 'Disable' (converts to regular folder).
key_points: can set password, expiration, storage limit
actual_response:
A Drop Box in kDrive is a feature that allows you to invite contacts to deposit content (files or folders) directly into your kDrive. The deposited content is then directly sent and classified in the specified location on your kDrive.

**How to create a Drop Box:**

1. **Access kDrive**: Go to the Infomaniak kDrive Web app at [ksuite.infomaniak.com/kdrive](https://ksuite.infomaniak.com/kdrive).
2. **Navigate to the desired folder**: In the left sidebar, navigate to the folder where you want the deposited data to be stored. You can choose a personal folder (My Folder) for private data specific to your user, or an Organization Folder (shared folder) for data accessible to other users of your kDrive.
3. **Create a new Drop Box**:
   - Click on the blue **New** button in the top right corner.
   - Select **Drop Box** from the menu.
   - Enter a name for the drop box.
   - The full path to the location of this drop box is specified for your information.
   - Choose whether to restrict access to your user only, even if the drop box is located in an Organization Folder (shared folder).
   - Click on the blue **Create** button.

4. **Share the Drop Box**:
   - Click on **Share** to get the link to the drop box or send it by email to your contacts.
   - Customize the appearance of the drop box and set advanced options, such as receiving email notifications upon file deposit, protecting the folder with a password, adding an expiration date, or limiting storage space.

5. **Disable or modify a Drop Box**:
   - Go to the **Shares** section in the left sidebar and click on **Drop boxes**.
   - Right-click or use the action menu (⋮) to the right of the drop box you want to modify.
   - Click on **Disable** to cancel the share link without deleting the already shared data (the box will become a simple folder).
   - Click on **Settings** to modify the advanced options.

**Related Actions:**
- You can disable or modify a drop box at any time.
- The content uploaded by your contacts is directly sent and classified in the right place on your kDrive.
- You can choose to receive email notifications upon file deposit, protect the folder with a password, add an expiration date, or limit storage space.

**Platform Limitations:**
- Not all kDrive offers support Drop Boxes. Please refer to your specific offer's details.

**User Role Requirements:**
- Only users with access to the specified folder can deposit data into the drop box.
- The kDrive account owner can create, share, and manage drop boxes.

**Important Notes:**
- Data deposited into a drop box is directly sent and classified in the specified location on your kDrive.
- You can customize the appearance and set advanced options for the drop box.
- Drop Boxes are not available on iOS or Lite Sync.

question: How do I resolve sync conflicts in kDrive?
ground_truth: Sync conflicts occur when: a file is modified locally AND on kDrive Web simultaneously, or during conflicting create/move operations. Resolution: kDrive Web version is kept, local version is saved as '[filename]_conflict'. Options: 1) Keep both (only original syncs). 2) Delete _conflict if it's older. 3) Delete original and rename _conflict to sync it. 4) Manually merge then delete _conflict. To view conflicts: click kDrive icon > info button > view events. From version 3.6.11, locally modified files are moved to 'kDrive Rescue Folder' instead of deleted. Avoid conflicts by not working on the same file with multiple people.
key_points: conflicts when same file modified locally and online
can keep both, delete, or merge
actual_response:
To resolve sync conflicts in kDrive, follow these steps:

**Prerequisites:**
- You must have a kDrive account
- The conflicting files must be synced using kDrive Sync client

**How to use:**
1. Open the kDrive Sync client
2. Right-click on the folder with sync conflicts
3. Select "Resolve conflicts"

**Important notes:**
- kDrive will create copies of the conflicting files with "_conflict_YYYY-MM-DD_HH-mm-ss" appended to the filename
- Choose to keep the local or remote version, or click "Compare" to view differences and manually merge changes
- You can also resolve conflicts directly in your file explorer:
  - Windows: Under the "kDrive Sync" folder, navigate to "Conflict Files" and follow the same steps as above
  - macOS: Under the "kDrive Sync" folder, navigate to "Conflict Files" and follow the same steps as above

**Related actions:**
- After resolving conflicts, you can delete the unnecessary copies
- You can also configure kDrive to keep local copies of sync conflicts: Go to Preferences > Sync > Advanced > "Keep local copies of sync conflicts"

**Source:** [kDrive Sync documentation](https://docs.infomaniak.com/kdrive/sync/)

question: How do I manage user rights in kDrive?
ground_truth: kDrive has 2 permission levels: 1) Administrator - same rights as owner (sharing, statistics, restore/delete folders, import data, access all files). 2) User - access folders at root, create/share content, but cannot manage product, view statistics, or create root folders. To modify: 1) Go to ksuite.infomaniak.com/kdrive. 2) Click action menu next to the kDrive. 3) Click 'Manage users'. 4) Select user and choose access level. Note: Don't confuse Manager rights (product management) with kDrive rights (data access). A user can have restricted Manager rights but be Administrator in kDrive.
key_points: don't confuse Manager rights with kDrive rights
actual_response:
Here's how you can manage user rights in kDrive:

## Prerequisites
- The user must have an Infomaniak account.
- You must have a kDrive offer with available user quotas.

## How kDrive user permissions work
kDrive offers two levels of permissions for user access:
1. **Administrator**: Gives users the same rights as the kDrive owner, including sharing, statistics, activity reports, restoring and deleting folders, importing external data, etc.
2. **User**: Allows access to folders located at the root of the kDrive and managing and freely sharing their content.

## Manage a kDrive user's rights

### Via folder sharing
1. Access the kDrive Web app.
2. Select the relevant kDrive in the sidebar.
3. Click on the action menu (⋮) of the relevant folder or file.
4. Click on "Share".
5. Enter the user's email address and select the desired access level (Administrator or User).

### Via kDrive user management
1. Access the kDrive Web app.
2. Check or select the relevant kDrive in the sidebar.
3. Click on the action menu (⋮) located to the right of the relevant item.
4. Click on "Manage users".
5. Manage the desired user's rights, choose the desired access level (Administrator or User).

## Platform limitations
- The content of the "Organization Folders" directory is common and visible to other kDrive users.
- Contents shared by other users from their private part of the kDrive are not listed in the "Shares" menu of other users.
- Any folder or file can be shared with other kDrive users and the contacts of your choice.

## User role requirements
- To manage kDrive user rights, you must be a kDrive administrator.

## Related actions
- To learn more about managing user rights, see [this other guide](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2365).
- To manage kDrive users, see [this guide](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2364).

## Default behaviors
- The "General" channel exists by default.

## Related features
- To use AI for your files on kDrive, see [this guide](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2566/use-euria-on-kdrive).
- For a getting started guide with kDrive, see [this page](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2366/getting-started-guide-kdrive).

question: How can I access kDrive files locally without downloading them?
ground_truth: To access kDrive files locally: 1) Install the kDrive desktop app. 2) Click on the kDrive icon in notification area (top right macOS, bottom right Windows, double-click on Linux). 3) Click action menu at top right. 4) Choose 'Open kDrive Web' to access server files. 5) Or click the item above to open the local folder. Files can be physically present or virtually present (if Lite Sync is enabled). Lite Sync allows files to appear locally without taking up disk space - they download on demand when opened.
key_points: Open kDrive Web for server files
actual_response:
To access kDrive files locally without downloading them, you can use the following methods:

**Using WebDAV:**

1. **Prerequisites:** You must have a kDrive account and the WebDAV client of your choice (e.g., Cyberduck, Transmit, or the built-in WebDAV client in your operating system).
2. **Technical specifications:** WebDAV allows you to work with your files directly from your local machine as if they were stored locally. However, keep in mind that changes made locally will be reflected in the cloud, and vice versa.
3. **How to use:**
   - Open your WebDAV client.
   - Connect to `https://webdav.kdrive.infomaniak.com/your_email` (replace `your_email` with your actual email).
   - Enter your kDrive credentials when prompted.
   - Once connected, you will see your kDrive files and folders. You can now work with them as if they were stored locally on your machine.

**Using the kDrive desktop application:**

1. **Prerequisites:** You must have a kDrive account, and the kDrive desktop application installed on your computer.
2. **Platform limitations:** The kDrive desktop application is available for Windows, macOS, and Linux.
3. **Technical specifications:** The kDrive desktop application allows you to sync specific folders from your kDrive account to your local machine. Changes made locally or in the cloud will be synced automatically.
4. **How to use:**
   - Open the kDrive desktop application.
   - Log in to your kDrive account if you haven't already.

question: How do I create a channel in kChat?
ground_truth: To create a channel in kChat: 1) Click the button in the left sidebar of kChat web app (ksuite.infomaniak.com/kchat). 2) Click 'Create a new channel'. 3) Set: A) Name (modifiable later), B) URL (lowercase, numbers, dots, dashes, underscores), C) Private or Public status, D) Description. Every Organization has a default 'General' channel for all users. Public channels are visible to all; Private channels require invitation. To convert public to private: click channel > chevron > Convert (permanent). To leave: chevron > Leave. To archive: chevron > Archive. Can also add to favorites, mute, or organize by categories.
actual_response:
To create a channel in kChat, follow these steps:

- Prerequisites: You must be a moderator or an administrator of the workspace.
- Platform limitations: Channel creation is not available on the mobile app (iOS and Android).
- Technical specifications: There is no limit to the number of channels that can be created.
- User role requirements: Only moderators and administrators can create channels.
- Important warnings or notes: All members of the workspace can join and participate in channels.
- File types and extensions: Channels can contain text messages, files (documents, images, videos), and links.
- Default behaviors: A General channel is created by default when a new workspace is created.
- Related actions: Channel creators can add or remove members, make channels private or public, and delete channels.
- How to use: To create a new channel, click on the "+" icon in the channel list and select "Create a channel". Enter the channel name and description, then click "Create".

question: What slash commands are available in kChat?
ground_truth: To use slash commands in kChat: 1) Click in the composition field. 2) Type / followed by the command. 3) Send. Typing just / shows available commands in a modal (like going offline). You can create custom slash commands: 1) Open kChat web or desktop app. 2) Click 'New' icon next to organization name. 3) Click 'Integrations'. 4) Click 'Slash command'. 5) Add a command with name, trigger, content type, and action. Custom commands can call external APIs or run scripts. Note: External users cannot see the Integrations menu.
actual_response:
**kChat Slash Commands**

kChat offers several slash commands to enhance your chat experience. Here are the main ones:

**Go Offline**
- Command: `/away [message]`
- Use: Set your status to offline with an optional message.
- Related actions: `/back` to go back online.

**Manage Notifications**
- Command: `/notifications [on/off]`
- Use: Turn notifications on or off.
- Related actions: Manage notification settings in profile.

**Create a Poll**
- Command: `/poll [question] [option1] [option2] ...`
- Use: Create a poll with a question and up to 10 options.
- Related actions: Vote using reaction buttons, view results.

**Remind Me**
- Command: `/remind [time] [message]`
- Use: Set a reminder for a specific time with an optional message.
- Related actions: Reminders are sent to you directly.

**Create a Task**
- Command: `/task [title] [due date] [description]`
- Use: Create a task with a title, due date, and description.
- Related actions: View, edit, or delete tasks in the Tasks channel.

**Integrate External Apps**
- Command: `/integrate [app name]`
- Use: Integrate external apps using webhooks.
- Prerequisites: Not be an external user.
- Platform limitations: Not available on iOS.
- Related actions: Manage integrations in the Integrations menu.

**Custom Commands**
- Prerequisites: Not be an external user.
- User role requirements: Organization administrator.
- Platform limitations: Not available on iOS.
- Technical specifications: Requires configuration of expected content type and action to execute.
- Related actions: Create, edit, or delete custom commands in the Integrations menu.

**Invite an External User**
- Prerequisites: Not be an external user.
- Platform limitations: Not available on iOS.
- Technical specifications: External users have limited permissions.
- Related actions: Invite users via email or manage external users in the Integrations menu.

**Change Language**
- Prerequisites: None.
- Platform limitations: Not available on iOS.
- Technical specifications: Language is chosen for the Manager.
- Related actions: Change language in Infomaniak profile.

**Archive/Delete a Channel**
- Prerequisites: None.
- Platform limitations: Not available on iOS.
- Technical specifications: Archiving prevents new messages and doesn't count in channel quota. Deleting is permanent.
- Related actions: Archive, unarchive, or delete channels in the channel menu.

**Manage Members**
- Prerequisites: Administrator permissions.
- Platform limitations: Not available on iOS.
- Technical specifications: Invited users are listed as pending until registration is complete.
- Related actions: Invite, remove, or manage members in the channel menu.

**Voice Messages**
- Prerequisites: None.
- Platform limitations: Not available on iOS.
- Technical specifications: Voice messages can be up to 1 hour long.
- Related actions: Record, listen, or delete voice messages in the conversation.

**Default behaviors:**
- General channel exists by default.
- New users receive a welcome message.
- Guests have limited permissions.
- Reminders are sent directly to the user.
- Tasks are created in the Tasks channel.
- Voice messages stop when the meeting ends.

**Related actions:**
- Use `/` to see a list of available commands.
- Custom commands can be created and managed in the Integrations menu.
- External apps can be integrated using webhooks in the Integrations menu.
- Channel management can be done in the channel menu.
- User management can be done in the channel menu.
- Voice messages can be managed in the conversation.

*Source: [Infomaniak Documentation](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2134/using-kchat-slash-commands)*

question: How can I connect external applications to kChat?
ground_truth: To connect external apps to kChat using webhooks: 1) Open kChat web or desktop app. 2) Click 'New' icon next to organization name. 3) Click 'Integrations'. 4) Access webhook categories. For incoming webhooks (receive messages from external apps): 1) Click 'Incoming Webhooks'. 2) Add name and description. 3) Select destination channel. 4) Save to get URL. 5) External app sends POST request with JSON: {"text": "message"}. For outgoing webhooks: kChat sends info when events occur. Parameters include channel override, username, icon_url. Response includes message details. Add ?slack_return_format=true for Slack-style response.

question: How can I invite external users to kChat?
ground_truth: To invite external users to kChat: Prerequisites: Be Organization administrator with full kChat rights. Steps: 1) Access kChat at ksuite.infomaniak.com/kchat or desktop app. 2) Click 'Invite members' button. 3) Click link to invite new user. 4) Enter email address(es). 5) Specify channel(s) they'll access. 6) Click send invitation. Invited users receive email with link to the channel. They must create Infomaniak account if needed. External users are not counted as regular users. Guests CAN: pin messages, use slash commands, add favorites, mute, update profile. Guests CANNOT: discover public channels, join open teams, create DMs with non-channel members, invite people.
